title: CRL: signer_discovered flag's two-case semantics not obvious
description:
Location: pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs, CrlChecker struct field signer_discovered (lines 166-181)

The signer_discovered bool flag controls a critical behavioral branch in check_revocation: when true, the IndirectCrlIssuerMissing/Unexpected cross-check is bypassed (line 499-513). The field doc explains this at length (15 lines of comment), but the semantics are subtle:

  (Some(discovered), false) if self.signer_discovered => { ... }

A reader encountering this match arm must understand that 'false' means 'the CRL does NOT declare itself indirect' AND 'signer_discovered' means 'we found the signer via the discovery constructor, so we intentionally bypass the indirect/direct cross-check'. This is non-obvious correct behavior.

What goes wrong: a future contributor adding a new CrlChecker constructor could set crl_issuer_cert to Some(...) without understanding that signer_discovered controls whether the indirect-CRL cross-check fires. The comment is thorough but the flag name does not communicate 'bypass indirect-CRL validation'; something like bypass_indirect_check or signer_from_bundle would make the control flow self-documenting at the match site.
